summary: Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at the École Polytechnique, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA at Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger, later holding posts there and serving as Director of the Institute for Indology and Tamilistics at Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter Conrad (1932–2001) worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his Dr.iur. at Heidelberg University by 1963 and served as a Senior Research Fellow there from 1963 to 1997.

Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Calcutta and Marburg under Johannes Nobel and Wilhelm Rau, and held positions at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1967–1985) and Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1977–1985).

Dieter Gunkel is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Middlebury College and UCLA. He held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017) and University of Richmond (2017–2024), before becoming Associate Professor at UCLA in 2024.

Dieter Schlingloff studied at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and habilitated at Berlin. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, he held posts at Göttingen, Kiel University (1968–1971), and the University of Munich (1972–1996).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indology scholar who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau (attested 1970).

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at Cologne and Bonn under Shri Krishna Sharma. He completed his PhD and habilitation at Bonn, where he was an außerplanmäßiger Professor (1978–2007), and later directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Diether Lauenstein (1914–1990) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Ludwig Heller at Tübingen and Johannes Nobel at Marburg, later habilitating at the University of Greifswald, where he held a post in 1944.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He served as Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University (1968–2001).
Dieuke Gaastra was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University under Johan Hendrik Gallée and Willem Caland, completing a PhD in 1906.

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) was a scholar and figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Calcutta. He taught archaeology at Calcutta (1965–1977) and Delhi (1977–1990), and was Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and held posts at Visva-Bharati University and the University of Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D.Litt. from Patna University, and held a teaching post at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic posts at Virginia Commonwealth University (~2002–2017) and Ohio State University (attested 2006).

Dina Johanna Kohlbrugge (1911–1999) was an Indology and Iranian studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and served there as Professor of Modern Persian and Iranian language and literature (1949; 1956–1981).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, later serving there as Docent (1901) and Professor (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and was Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.
